name: Maine (United States, 1901–1909)

colors.symbolism: buff, the facing colour of the old colonial uniform
the pine tree of the Pine Tree State

description: A buff field bearing a green pine tree in the centre and a blue five-pointed star in the upper hoist.
history: Maine's first official state flag, adopted 21 March 1901 and credited to Adjutant General John T. Richards. The statute specified a field 'buff, charged with the emblem of the State, a pine tree proper in the center, and the polar star (a mullet of five points), in blue in the upper corner.' It served as both the state and the militia flag and was shown at the 1904 St. Louis Exposition, but was replaced on 24 February 1909 by the present coat-of-arms flag. Only one contemporary specimen is known, a small silk flag of about 1908. The design was revived commercially from the 1990s and a modernised version was put to Maine voters as Question 5 in November 2024, which was rejected.

features.symbolism: the state motto Dirigo, 'I lead', and Maine's place as the northernmost state
